AUTHOR: Jahanbakht
TITLE: Linking fish activity and turbidity through visual and sensor data fusion and deep learning
REGION: Port of Mackay, northern Queensland, Australia (11 m depth), March-May 2023
DATA: Own fixed PTZ camera stills with co-located IMO NTU turbidity logger; 29,349 daytime images (9331 with valid NTU), binary fish presence labels by volunteers (1519 fish-present instances)
V_EV: Section 3.1: 'images with valid NTU values were categorized into five turbidity levels ... corresponding respectively to maximum values of 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 NTU.' (detector metrics reported only overall, Table 1)
D2: Fish detector zero-shot (no training split); turbidity CNN: 9331 images split 60/40 train/validation (5598/3733), unit not stated
D_EV: no statement found on the split unit; Section 4.2: 'all 9331 images with valid turbidity values were divided into a training set of 5598 images (60 %) and a validation set of 3733 images (40 %).'
R_EV: Section 3.2.1: 'The YOLOWorld models used in this study were employed in a zero-shot setting without any additional fine-tuning or re-training.'
C_EV: no statement found on a detection confidence threshold or detection uncertainty; FP only discussed via precision/specificity ('YOLOWorld-v2 XLarge had better precision and specificity, suggesting it excelled at reducing False Positives')
E_EV: Section 4.3: 'we examined the correlation between the fish count in our dataset and the corresponding turbidity levels'; detector evaluated against volunteer labels: 'Each image was binary labeled as either fish present or fish absent'
ARCH: YOLO-World v1 Large / v2 XLarge zero-shot open-vocabulary detector (prompt 'fish') + custom lightweight CNN regressor for image-based NTU estimation; polynomial regression of fish count vs turbidity
METR: Image-level accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1, confusion matrix; turbidity RMSE, bias, scatter index, prediction/confidence intervals; R2 of count-turbidity regressions
NOTE: Turbidity measured in NTU, depth 11 m, daytime-only images, but detector performance is not stratified by turbidity (V6=N, V_ALL=P per rule); the count-turbidity regression relates detected fish counts (not detection performance) to NTU, and detectability decline with turbidity is not separated from ecology (V7=N). R1=Y because the generically pretrained detector is applied zero-shot to a new underwater domain; no in-domain baseline reported (R3=N). Turbidity CNN reports 70% prediction intervals with ~86% empirical coverage, but this is uncertainty for the turbidity covariate, not for fish detection/counting; coded C3/C2=없음 (verifier: could be argued as C3/C2 '기타'). Detector pretraining is Objects365/GQA/CC3M (not an allowed PRE value), coded NR. E2/E5 based on agreement with volunteer binary presence labels of the same images; E4=FNR from confusion matrix FN 8.6%. Port waters do not fit ENV options, coded NR. Publication year 2025 online / 2026 issue.
